newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Smurfit chief urges Irish EMU membership.
newsitem.headline: Smurfit chief urges Irish EMU membership.

text.p: The President of Irish paper and packaging manufacturer Jefferson Smurfit Group plc said on Thursday that Ireland should join European economic and monetary union (EMU) irrespective of Britain's decision.

"Let us have the vision and independence to pursue the correct decision of joining, regardless of the UK position," PJ Wright told a Dublin business seminar. "Let us work together with our European colleges to make a political and financial success of the euro and thereby ensure the participation of our largest trading partner (Britain)," said Wright.

Wright said that Ireland delayed joining until Britain did, it risked a serious reduction in foreign investment because international firms could decide to locate in other EU countries to eliminate currency exposure.
A collapse or delay in EMU would undo recent falls of the German mark against other major currencies and turn it into Europe's main reserve currency.

It would be persistently over-valued, which would damage exports and nip Germany's fledgling economic recovery in the bud," he said. Wright said that if Germany's economic revival faltered, it would be very difficult for Ireland to maintain its current level of growth, currently among the EU's highest. He said that any delay in implementing EMU would "be close to fatal."

Wright told his audience that EMU should lead to a liquid bond market similar that existing in the United States. The Irish corporate bond market was not well developed and companies relied too much on bank markets, he said.

Wright welcomed the future enlargement of the European Union because it would mean a bigger market for Irish goods and services and additional human resources bringing new skills and energy into Europe.
